entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Shanghai was a pivotal conflict in the Second Sino-Japanese War, fought between the Nationalist Government of China and the Imperial Japanese Army. 

 This battle took place from August 13 to November 26, 1937, in the city of Shanghai, which was a key urban center in East Asia. 

 The battle was a crucial turning point in the war, as it led to the fall of Shanghai and the subsequent occupation of the city by Japanese forces. 

 The consequences of the battle were far-reaching, as it not only led to the loss of life and destruction of property but also marked a significant shift in the balance of power in East Asia, paving the way for further Japanese expansion in the region.

 As Japanese forces continued their advance, they would eventually capture the city of Nanking, leading to the infamous Nanking Massacre, a dark chapter in modern history.
